properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/20/2025
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 8245729
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2025
Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4014690 and violations issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a production fluid, frack chemical and fresh water mixture.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, there appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department did not observe the trench previously observed to be bordering the secondary containment in the release area during IR 4014690. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.75mS, 0.48mS, and 0.44mS . These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-08 to Pleasant Oil & Gas in Pleasant Twp, Warren county. OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pleasant Oil & Gas
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-08
Violation Code: OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
Violation ID: 886652
Permit API: 123-48276
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-08
Comments: Narrative: On 8 June 2020, Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (Department) Water Quality Specialist Mark Madeley (Madeley) and Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Rich Sheriff (Sheriff) conducted a routine/complete inspection (inspection) of the Oakland 11 OG Well (well) in order to determine compliance with the Oil and Gas Act and the applicable technical regulations in 25 Pa. Code Chapters 78 & 102. The following was observed during the Department's inspection: 1. The well was stable and producing, with the pit having been previously reclaimed. The 23 December 2019 inspection of the site indicated that the area was, ‘snow covered and stable…appeared that temporary stabilisation measures will need to be used when weather allows'. 2. Madeley and Sheriff observed a lack of uniform vegetative cover at the site - with no evidence of seed or mulch having been placed. The pit appeared to have deformities as well and was not shaped in such a way as to prevent the pooling of water. 3. Madeley and Sheriff noted the presence of a well permit attached to a nearby tree but no evidence of a site tag on the pump jack or wellhead. 4. Mr James Highhouse arrived on-site during the inspection and told Sheriff and Madeley that he was going to immediately lay mulch about the area. Mr Highhouse also made reference to the presence of a mini-excavator already near the site and said he would be using the machine to grade the pit area for better stabilisation. 5. Sheriff and Madeley expressed their intention to have a look at other wells in the area whilst inspecting and Mr Highhouse said he would be attaching site tags to the Oakland 11 and other nearby pump jacks immediately. Madeley and Sheriff observed Mr Highhouse attaching signs to the Oakland 11 and Oakland 12 (123-48277) pump jacks. The Department has reviewed the observations of Madeley and requests the following information be submitted prior to 17 July 2020: 1. Evidence confirming the pit area has been better shaped to resist pooling of water and erosion See below under REMARKS/VIOLATIONS: PA Code Title 25, Chapter 78.53 & 102.4 (b) (1) and PA Code Title 58, Oil & Gas Act, Chapter 32, 3216 (b): During and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including…producing…the operator shall design, implement and maintain best management practises; [T]he following erosion and sediment control requirements apply…implementation and maintenance of E&S BMPs are required to minimise the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation 2. Evidence confirming mulch has been spread about the area in order to facilitate further vegetative reclamation which will lead to >70% uniform vegetative cover See below under REMARKS/VIOLATIONS: PA Code Title 25, 102.22: Permanent stabilisation. Upon final completion of an earth disturbance activity…top-soil restored, replaced, or amended, seeded, mulched or otherwise permanently stabilised and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation; Clean Streams Law, Section 402 (b) The requested documentation can be faxed to my attention at 814 723 0964, sent via e-mail to mamadeley@pa.gov or posted to the following address: ¿Mark Madeley ¿DEP- Bureau of District Oil and Gas Operations ¿Northwest District -Warren Office ¿321 North State Street ¿Warren, PA 16365 If you have any questions, please contact Mark Madeley at 814 308 3118. On 15 June 2020, a copy of this narrative was sent (in SAIR application) via e-mail to JRHOIL69@msn.com, afterwards Madeley also phoned Mr Highhouse at 814 688 1443

Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 957716
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Cnx Gas Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2018-12-07
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 836270
Permit API: 059-27587
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Richhill Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2018-12-07
Comments: On December 7, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site. The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a follow up inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad on 12/1/18, and violations issued on 12/3/18. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was also excavating the PCSM and PCSM collection channel at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites during the 12/3/18 inspection. The operator has completed hydraulic fracturing operations on the site and has begun removing the equipment necessary for hydraulic fracturing from the well pad. The operator has reported to the Department that secondary containment will be setup on the well pad to store excavated, impacted soils for disposal and remediation efforts will continue all weekend and into next week on the well pad as well as in the PCSM structures impacted by the reuse water spill.

Inspection Date: 7/14/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) on 7/14/2025 at 0630 hours. The weather ranged from mid-70s to mid-80s degrees throughout the day. The inspection was conducted in response to a report of a well control incident occurring on the 7H well which resulted in a release of produced fluids. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390569 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, at ~1830 hours on 7/13/2025 a pressure issue on the 7H well caused the uncontrolled release of produced fluid up the casing[s] to the pad surface. Efforts to control pressure and prevent the escaping fluids have failed so far. Secondary containments were overtopped and fluid has and continues to escape the pad surface. A temporary berm was constructed along the northwestern edge around the western corner of the pad, below the fill slope, to collect fluids (photos #3 to 5). The "corner" berm below the fill slope was said to be completed around 0000 hours on 7/14/2025. Numerous gravel berms were constructed on the pad surface to help prevent fluids from escaping the pad surface but are failing in numerous spots. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed sheet flowing from numerous areas along the southwestern edge of the pad (see photo #8 for example). Fluid observed in the western corner of the stormwater control basin was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned a reading of >19.99mS/cm. ~1000 hours: A Repsol representative onsite indicated that larger pumps were en route to catch up on fluid collection that is being pooled on the western corner of the well pad (photo #9). According to Repsol, the pumps being brought in should be able to catch up on the fluid that is pooled on the surface.A secondary berm/trench was constructed below the first "corner" berm below the fill slope sometime throughout the day. A break in the first berm was dug to allow fluid collected to flow into the secondary berm. The secondary berm is flowing fluid into the stormwater control basin onsite (see photos #10-12).Fluid was able to reach the stormwater control basin shown in photo #7. The DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the basin which was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (Sample #0983-510).A third (tertiary) berm/trench was later constructed below the secondary berm and was built into the stormwater control basin. The short side wall of the basin was removed to allow for excess fluid build-up in the basin to collect in the third berm. The secondary and tertiary berms are utilized to relieve hydrostatic pressure from the "corner" berm. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed on the pad surface, in the constructed berms, in the pad's stormwater channels and in the stormwater control basin. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were observed directly down-gradient of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm and along the installed surface waterline. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were also observed along the surface waterline in the field adjacent to the pad (photo #13).Repsol identified and initiated the screening and sampling of nearby water supplies as required by 25 Pa. Code 78a.66b(4).Based on the findings of this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, SWMA 301 and Clean Streams Law 401. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.55(f) is cited against API #015-23892 as immediately corrected.I departed the well pad at 1430 hours.

Violations of Clean Streams Law 402, Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a) were issued but have been immediately corrected.

Comments: On January 4, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well site in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and DEP OGI Patrick Hiles. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3453961, during which remediation efforts were made by the operator in response to IR 3446144, where impacted soil was discovered by the Department.The following was observed:The well site excavation has been backfilled since IR 3453961 (see photos 2 and 5). The site appeared to be stabile with no concerns related to accelerated erosion or sedimentation, and was mulched and seeded. The excavation stockpile remains placed atop a sheet of black plastic (see photo 1). However, it was uncovered unlike the operator and contractor reported. The well head was equipped with a well tag (see photo 3). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of leaks or discharge (see photo 4). Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation stockpile to ensure that contamination has not leached into the ground. Elevated conductivity was found immediately downslope of the stockpile, on its west side (see photos 6, 7, and 9). Additional readings were taken approximately 4 feet further downslope from this point, and around the rest of the stockpile (see photos 8, 10, 11, and 12). No additional elevated readings were gathered. Soil conductivity readings were also taken in the backfilled area around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to the surrounding soil (see photos 13, 14, and 15). A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 170 Microsiemens (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been excavated from the area of release. However, the contaminants contained within the excavation stockpile appear to be washing downslope into the surrounding soil, and is therefore not being properly stored and/or contained. Because this contamination appears to be localized close to the stockpile, the Department recommends immediate remediation and proper storage to prevent the contamination from spreading. Also, the Department once again requests an approximate quantity released from the brine tank, and the waste manifest when available.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MINARD RUN OIL CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/22/2025
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8259790
Permit API: 053-26767
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Dan McCamey, of Minard Run Oil Company (MROC) on December 22, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred at Warrant 5107 Well #25P (API# 053-26767). A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

While inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I met Seneca's Ian Thom who described upcoming operations as follows: A vent pipe sticking from the ground and connected to the well casing may have been jarred during construction activities, causing the well to start bubbling. A Plants and Goodwin well servicing rig is mobilizing to the site to pump cement downhole. A secondary containment structure has been installed around the wellhead and two frac tanks remain on site, staged in secondary containment.I met Seneca's Jim Westfield on the north pad who described current operations as follows: The five newly drilled and completed wells are staged for flow-back. Two sand separators were attached to each wellhead. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Six frac tanks were staged north of the wellheads for flowback operations. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads.28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. Jim was unsure if these would be left on site for the next round of drilling and completion.Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Due to frozen conditions during this inspection, conductivity readings were not taken. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. As recommended in the inspections listed above, the DEP continues to recommend pursuing Act 2 for the large amount of elevated conducted fluids discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin.The DEP recommends the following: 1. Continue to determine the cause of elevated conductance discovered during previous inspections to prevent future occurrences. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.I left the site at 1525 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/9/2019 @1015 hours. The weather was 72 degrees and sunny, humidity 73%, no wind. Activity onsite consists of Tilden Marcellus finishing plumbing in the recently completed wells and removing the temporary flow back equipment. Jenn Compton and Taylor Parsons, Tilden Marcellus/Rockdale were present onsite for the inspection. As of today's inspection most of the secondary containment and rig mats have been removed. Tilden Marcellus is currently performing screening and removal of pad material impacted by stimulation activities, and the reported release on 6/3/2019. Ms. Compton stated in addition to the eastern pad edge and fill slope, an area in the center of the pad was found to have material with an elevated conductivity. The removed material was observed stockpiled in secondary containment, and covered in tarps. Trucks were observed removing fluid from the tank farm located along the northern cut slope. Fluid with an elevated conductivity was observed in both layers of secondary containment. A puddle/muddy area against the foam berm (photo#6) had a field measured conductivity of 3.28mS/cm. Mr. Parsons was notified of my findings regarding the tank farm. He stated a site truck was being dispatched to clean out the containments, and additional containment would be constructed in the truck load area to prevent spills to the ground surface from hose breaks. Tilden Marcellus ceased hauling and storage of fluids when notified of the violations. A NOV response was received on 7/9/2019. Violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301 and 25 Pa Code 78a56(a), cited 6/4/2019 in IR#2889847, remain OUTSTANDING against API#117-20478 from a previous release. Site remediation is ongoing. Once a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review, and attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed, the outstanding violations will be closed. No additional violations are cited at this time. Please ensure any deficiencies noted are addressed and contact me with any questions. I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Comments: On March 6, 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to WQS referral in IR 3721238.Access road is heavily saturated in water appearing to cause rutting issues from vehicle traffic. The Department recommends maintaining access road in a manner that allows vehicles to enter site. Violation issued for rutting. Well site is adequately vegetated.Well appears equipped for production. Well is tagged and posted with previous and new operator; pending the transfer currently under review by the Department, the "previous" operator, Questa Petro Co, remains operator at this time according to Department records.While on site, the Department observed active bubbling coming from the top of the well tree shown in Photo 13. Requesting OGI follow up.The leaking of the brine tank identified in IR 3721238 was observed on site shown in Photos 7-8. Specific conductivity readings were recorded as shown in Photos 9-12:- Background: 167.3 uS- On ground below corroded flange: 588 uS- On ground below open line: 820 uS- On ground below valve at well head: 391 uSThese readings indicate that a brine release has occurred on site. The Department recommends removing all impacted soil and properly disposing. The Department requests that the quantity released, composition of fluids released, how the release occurred, and when the release occurred is included in the NOV response. The Department requests disposal documents of the impacted material removed from the site, when made available. Violations issued for brine release.The Department has observed a trend in well sites that are being transferred from Questa Petro Co to Mountain V where the Questa well tags, and associated electrical tape, are being removed and left on site resulting in littering (Photo 4). The Department recommends properly disposing of trash.

Comments: On 6/07/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at theCessna 1 OG Wellsite, for violations cited on 5/6/2024 (Inspection ID:3757306, Enforcement ID:428752).Violations includedViolations of 102.11(a), 102.4(b)1, 102.22(b)1, 102.22(a), and 78.53.The following was observed:-The access road was not passable by vehicle. properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 9/22/2022 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Clearfield Twp, Cambria county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 9/22/2022
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 969141
Permit API: 021-21027
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Clearfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/22/2022
Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Brzez/Hum 3 well conducted on 09/22/2022. Arrived on location at 12:58. Violations were issued as a result of a 03/23/2022 site inspection (Inspection Record 3337145) for the following: OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to monitor well granted Inactive Status on an annual basis and submit monitoring reports. 78.104 - Failure to meet the terms of Inactive Status. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect each well for compliance with requirements. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit Mechanical Integrity Report to the Department. OGA3211(G) - Failure to post the permit number and operators info at the well site. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install the permit number on the well upon completion in a permanent manner. These concerns were also addressed in an email from the Department that was sent to the operator as a result of a 3/30/2021 site inspection (Inspection Record 3169298). A response from the operator was requested by the Department to discuss issues on site. No corrective actions were taken by the operator. This 9/22/2022 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition as the previous inspections. Violations were not addressed or responded to. Well is not equipped for production. Pumpjack, meter, and electric boxes remain on site. Much of the equipment has been dismantled. Wellhead is no longer tied inline. No permit number or operator ID found on the well. Wellhead and much of the equipment is overgrown with weeds/brush. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 04/15/2020. Operator failed to plug or return the well to active status. Review found no annual integrity monitoring reports submitted to the Department. All of the above violations remain outstanding.
